instructions:
# OIDC Service Provider

Hand-crafted skill for integrating an application as an OIDC service provider.

## What this skill does

- Discovers IdP endpoints from the well-known configuration
- Exchanges authorization codes for tokens
- Fetches userinfo and validates signatures with JWKS

## When to use

- Wiring a new app into corporate SSO as the SP side
- Debugging token endpoint failures
- Verifying user claims after login

## Real commands

```bash
# Discovery: find all endpoints dynamically
curl -s https://idp.example.com/.well-known/openid-configuration | jq -r '.authorization_endpoint, .token_endpoint, .jwks_uri'

# Exchange the authorization code
curl -s -X POST https://idp.example.com/token -d "grant_type=authorization_code&code=$CODE&redirect_uri=https://app.example.com/cb&client_id=app1&client_secret=$CLIENT_SECRET" | jq -r .access_token

# Read the user's claims
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://idp.example.com/userinfo | jq

# Inspect signing keys
curl -s https://idp.example.com/.well-known/jwks.json | jq -r '.keys[].kid'
```

## SP checklist

- Redirect to the authorization_endpoint with scope=openid profile email
- Validate the id_token signature against JWKS and the issuer claim
- Use userinfo only for non-critical profile data

## Testing

```bash
curl -s https://idp.example.com/.well-known/openid-configuration | jq -r '.token_endpoint'
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://idp.example.com/userinfo | jq '.email'
```

## Best practices

- Never hardcode endpoints; resolve them from discovery
- Store client_secret server-side only
- Cache JWKS and refresh on kid changes

examples.input: Set up login with my company IdP
examples.output: Read /.well-known/openid-configuration for endpoints, register client_id/redirect_uri, then exchange the code at the token endpoint and read userinfo.
Check the code was used once, redirect_uri matches exactly, and the client secret is current: replay with curl -X POST -d "grant_type=authorization_code&code=...".
